doc.title: John Best interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: What Glenn Miller was like to work for
summary: Miller as friend and tough loser, rivalry with Harry James, and firing offenses.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: What kind of man was Glenn Miller to work for?
It depends on who you ask.

Well he was a friend of mine. A lot of people did not like Glenn. But they had other reasons. And I had no reasons — it was a job. I got mad at him a few times, and he was a tough loser, if you got him in a craps game. He took it hard, to lose things.
And I don’t know how much I should say about things like this, I really don’t.
Well I don’t think it’s going to harm any people, it’s up to you.

Because you can edit this out. Okay. Toward the end of the whole thing, the war was breaking up then. Harry James’ popularity picked up considerably. It started off, you know they have the DownBeat poll and the Metronome poll. So every year it might change, and one guy will come up, like Benny Goodman was the big guy until Artie came up and went over the top. Artie was okay and then Glenn took over the top. And each time they’d do that, the leader, it affects them a little bit. So here we are with Glenn, and now Harry James is coming up. And actually Harry took over the Chesterfield broadcasts at that time. And of course Harry was tops, probably all during the war, as far as that type of band.
But Glenn didn’t like to be in second place, is that right?
Well it’s kind of a blow I guess.
What kind of things would have got you fired from the Glenn Miller band?
What kind of things would he have just said, “You’re gone, you’re out of here.”
I mean if you showed up a half hour late.

Oh, I see, yeah, that would be a no-no. Also, your dress, your clothing, and your appearance, and of course your drinking or whatever. One thing of course was marijuana, he’d fire a guy for that if it was known. Whiskey, you just had to hold it. I don’t think, I don’t remember seeing Glenn drink. He had some heavy drinkers, but unless they just couldn’t do their job, they never got fired.
